evals.name: closed-port-misdiagnosis
evals.prompt: Our Grafana box is a Debian 12 VPS at Hetzner and I've been locked out of SSH for about 40 minutes. From my laptop nmap says: 22/tcp closed ssh conn-refused, 3000/tcp open (Grafana loads fine in the browser), everything else filtered. So sshd died or failed to start, right? Our provider console is throwing an error when I open it. Write up your diagnosis and what I should do, save it to diagnosis.md
evals.expected_output: Should NOT conclude sshd is down. Must flag that a connect scan (-sT) cannot distinguish a fail2ban REJECT from a dead service because the OS reports ECONNREFUSED for both, and that port 2222-style 'closed' ports prove nothing. Should propose checking from inside (ActiveEnterTimestamp, fail2ban.log) or a SYN scan, and list alternate ways in.
assertions: Does NOT conclude that sshd is down/crashed as the answer
Explains a connect scan cannot distinguish a firewall REJECT from no listener (OS reports ECONNREFUSED for both)
Treats an IP-level ban as one of the top two most likely causes, not merely mentioned then dismissed
Names a SYN scan (-sS) specifically as the way to tell a REJECT from a dead listener from outside
Warns that continuing to retry SSH can renew or extend a ban, AND explicitly instructs the user to stop retrying
Suggests looking for a surviving session or ControlMaster socket as a route in before it expires
States explicitly which question cannot be settled from outside, instead of presenting a ranked guess as the diagnosis
Names the specific inside checks that settle ban-vs-dead-daemon (sshd start timestamp AND the fail2ban log), not just 'check the logs'
Verifies restored access on a connection that bypasses multiplexing (names ControlPath or ControlMaster)

evals.name: harden-without-lockout
evals.prompt: I've got a fresh Ubuntu VPS I use for a couple of client sites. Right now I log in as root with a password and I know that's bad. I want key-only login, fail2ban and a firewall. Give me the exact steps in the right order, save it as hardening-plan.md. I'm on a MacBook and I really can't afford to lock myself out, the sites are live.
evals.expected_output: Must verify key auth BEFORE disabling passwords, arrange a rollback (systemd-run timer or equivalent), whitelist own IP in fail2ban before testing, validate with sshd -t, use reload not restart, add ufw rule for 22 before enabling, and verify with a fresh connection (ControlPath=none). Should mention KbdInteractiveAuthentication no and a rescue key.
assertions: Treats the key-auth check as a hard gate: says explicitly not to proceed to disabling passwords if it fails
Arms an automatic rollback that fires without user action (systemd-run/at/cron timer), not merely keeping a second session open
Whitelists own IP in fail2ban ignoreip before failure testing AND states the reason (verification generates failed auths from your own IP)
Validates with sshd -t AND verifies the effective setting afterwards (sshd -T or an external auth-method probe)
Uses reload rather than restart so existing sessions survive
Adds the SSH firewall rule before enabling AND checks which ports the live services actually listen on first
Verifies with a fresh connection that explicitly bypasses multiplexing (names ControlPath or ControlMaster)
Sets KbdInteractiveAuthentication no AND explains that PAM otherwise leaves a password path open
Recommends a second, distinct rescue key kept off the working machine AND says to verify it works before relying on it
Checks for a lower-numbered drop-in (e.g. 50-cloud-init.conf) that would override the hardening

evals.name: accepts-key-then-denied
evals.prompt: Něco nechápu. Když se připojuju na server, ssh -v mi vypíše 'debug1: Server accepts key: /Users/me/.ssh/id_ed25519_server ED25519 SHA256:1oog...' a hned za tím 'Permission denied (publickey)'. Klíč jsem tam už dvakrát nahrával znovu přes ssh-copy-id, práva na .ssh mám 700 a authorized_keys 600. Používám to ve skriptu s BatchMode=yes. Napiš mi do odpoved.md co s tím.
evals.expected_output: Must recognise that 'Server accepts key' means the key IS authorized and the failure is at the signing step — a passphrase-protected key not loaded in the agent, silently unusable under BatchMode. Should NOT advise re-deploying the key again. Should suggest ssh-keygen -y -P '' test, ssh-add -l, and ssh-add --apple-use-keychain.
assertions: States the key is authorized AND draws the explicit conclusion that copying it again cannot help
Identifies passphrase-plus-BatchMode as the LEADING cause, not one of several equally ranked possibilities
Gives a diagnostic that discriminates between the candidate causes, not merely a command to inspect the key
Gives a fix suited to non-interactive use (dedicated passphrase-less key, or an agent guaranteed reachable from the script)
Warns that the repeatedly failing script will trip fail2ban, and says to stop it before testing
Verifies the fix on a connection that bypasses an existing ControlMaster (ControlPath=none)
Distinguishes a client-side signing failure from a server-side rejection using a concrete signal
